_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. status: active = connector-only, a reprint would clobber it; upstreamed = also fixed in the press, a reprint from a fixed press regenerates it, but the back-port must still be present today.

handfixes.summary: The `feedback` parent command carries an Example block, with the read-only `list` subcommand leading
handfixes.why: The press feedback parent template ships without an Examples section, which the Phase 5 dogfood gate flags as a finding. The example was hand-added and `list` deliberately leads so the first thing an operator copies is read-only rather than a write. A reprint from an unfixed press template drops the block and the dogfood finding returns.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Add an Examples section to the press `feedback` parent template so it is emitted by construction (filed as a retro item against the generator).

handfixes.summary: `software get-installer-setup` declares typed exit codes 0,3 so a 404 is a not-found answer rather than a command failure
handfixes.why: A vendor/package-manager pair with no installer setup configured on the tenant returns HTTP 404. Without the `pp:typed-exit-codes` annotation the generated command surfaces that as a generic failure, so an agent cannot distinguish 'this pair needs no setup' from 'the call broke'. Generated endpoint commands do not currently derive typed exit codes from declared 404 responses, so a reprint reverts this to an untyped failure. Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02): re-applied on the 4.35.1 annotation map (pp:requires-input/pp:happy-args).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Derive `pp:typed-exit-codes` from the operation's declared 404 response in the press so endpoint commands get this by construction (filed as a retro item against the generator).

handfixes.summary: the MCP tenant gate falls through to the tool handler when no platform source is registered, instead of default-denying every non-mirror tool
handfixes.why: cli.VerifyMCPInvocation returns (nil, nil) when registeredPlatformSource is nil, which means 'there is nothing to gate' - and no connector in this repo registers a platform source (registerPlatformSource has zero callers outside internal/cli/platform_client.go). The 4.30.1/4.30.2 gate read that nil session as a failure and answered 'MCP tenant gate is not configured' for every tool that is not a Cobra mirror. Cobra mirrors carry pp:tenant-gate = "child-cli" and pass through, so the damage was invisible in a tool count: 6 tools per connector were dead while the server still listed them. Those 6 are the entire offline-mirror surface (context, search, sql) plus the entire code-orchestration surface (<prefix>_search / _get / _execute) - exactly the capabilities this connector's own description says a plain read-only MCP does not ship. Measured over stdio before the fix: 6/6 returned isError with the gate message; after, all 6 reach their handler. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press 4.30.3 (issue #4157, PR #4171); this is the surgical back-port, byte-identical to what 4.30.3 emits. TestMCPUngatedInvocationUsesRealVerifier is the regression test that ships with the 4.30.3 template: it drives the wrapper with the REAL verifier (not the fake the other two tests install) and fails if the handler is blocked. Reverting either the fall-through or the test fails check_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already fixed in the press at 4.30.3 (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4171). A reprint on 4.30.3 or later regenerates both the fall-through and the conformance test, so this entry exists to keep the back-port from being dropped by a reprint on an older engine or by a regen-merge that resurrects the 4.30.2 body.

asserts.not_contains: NewToolResultError("MCP tenant gate is not configured")

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For cork the manifest gained: CORK_BASE_URL, CORK_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. server.json gained: CORK_BASE_URL, CORK_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: CORK_BASE_URL, CORK_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: cli/NOTICE names this connector's contributor, in the Apache-2.0 attribution channel
handfixes.why: CONTRIBUTING.md and the public contributing page promise that a contributor's credit survives a regeneration. Nothing enforced that. The press regenerates cli/NOTICE from its own template, which carries the CLI Printing Press attribution but not this repo's per-connector 'contributed by' sentence, so a reprint would silently delete the only place the credit lives. PR #283 moved contributor credit out of per-file copyright headers and into NOTICE, which makes this line the load-bearing copy rather than a duplicate. Pinning the exact sentence here is what turns the promise into a checked one.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The press has no per-connector contributor field, so there is nothing to encode upstream today. If one is added, the NOTICE template should emit this sentence by construction. Related: the press stamps the copyright header from whoever ran the generator, filed as mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4326 closed 2026-08-25 as not planned (wontfix: operator-stamped attribution is product/config work), no fix landed; this hand-fix is permanent unless re-filed; do NOT cite #4326 as open.

asserts.contains: The Cork connector was contributed by Abhi Saini (@geekbrownbear).

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it. Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02): still needed: 4.35.1 recall records hit/miss events and playbook list appends an audit record.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, `analytics` included, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: software install (POST /software/installer/install).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.why: Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02): work order: an MCP write must preview and send only with confirm: true. The published build sent integrations_delete, software_install and the other endpoint writes on the first call. internal/mcp/cork_endpoint_confirm.go RequireConfirmForEndpointWrites (gradient precedent) wraps every registered tool that lacks the read-only hint and is not a mirrored command, so a later endpoint is gated too. Wired by ONE line in GENERATED internal/mcp/tools.go after cobratree.RegisterAll: a regeneration drops it. Proven both ways: unwired, TestEndpointWriteSendsOnlyWithConfirm saw the DELETE reach the stub server with no confirm and TestRegisteredWritesNeedConfirm listed the writes ungated; wired, 0 requests until confirm is boolean true (nil, false, "true" and 1 all preview), then exactly 1.

handfixes.why: Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02): work order. internal/mcp/cobratree/cork_confirm.go RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (cisco-duo 4.35.1 shape, no --apply commands on cork) fails closed: only read-only tools, mcp:local-write commands and the local-only list run ungated. handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. The credential store, config and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own layer (the 0.1.8 secret-echo funnel, which the 4.35.1 reprint dropped; not a `retired` record because check_handfixes.py accepts only registry-backed retirements). Classes closed, each by a built-binary test seen failing first on the pre-kit build (.review/red-first-kit.txt): an API error that echoes the key, a piece of it, base64 or URL-encoded (TestAPIErrorEchoOfKeyIsWithheld, CLI, --agent and MCP); an unconfirmed MCP integrations_connect preview that echoed credential_fields (TestMCPConnectPreviewWithholdsCredentialFields); --credential-fields held before the flag parser (TestCLICredentialFieldsFlagHeld); a profile value under a credential flag held at startup (TestProfileCredentialValueHeldAtStartup); a held credential refused to another origin and over plain http (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP); SPACEFAST_TOKEN held (TestSpacefastTokenHeld); the learn journal and the feedback ledger never record a held credential (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential, TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded). A malformed config's key stays held at startup (TestMalformedConfigCredentialHeldAtStartup, a guard: the press already passed it). In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the seams swap (credkit_seam_test.go in cli, mcp, client). The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to the _length_limit DSN parameter, and openReadOnlySQLite runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).
